name: authentication-best-practices
description: Enforce secure authentication patterns: password hashing, session management, MFA support, and token handling
author: community
content:
## Authentication Best Practices

Authentication is the front door. Get it wrong and nothing else matters (OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures).

### Password Storage
- NEVER store passwords in plaintext or reversible encryption
- Use bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2id — nothing else
- bcrypt: minimum cost factor 10 (12+ preferred)
- Argon2id: minimum 19 MiB memory, 2 iterations, 1 parallelism
- NEVER use MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, or any plain hash for passwords — even with salt
- Generate a unique random salt per password (bcrypt/argon2 do this automatically)

### Session Management
- Generate session IDs with a cryptographically secure random generator (minimum 128 bits of entropy)
- Regenerate session ID after login to prevent session fixation
- Set session cookies: `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`)
- Implement absolute session timeout (e.g., 24 hours) and idle timeout (e.g., 30 minutes)
- Invalidate sessions server-side on logout — do not just clear the cookie
- Store sessions server-side; do not put sensitive data in client-side tokens alone

### JWT / Token-Based Auth
- Use short-lived access tokens (5-15 minutes)
- Use opaque refresh tokens stored server-side with rotation
- Always validate: issuer (`iss`), audience (`aud`), expiration (`exp`), algorithm (`alg`)
- NEVER allow `alg: none` — explicitly set the expected algorithm
- Store signing keys in secrets management, not in code
- Do not store JWTs in localStorage — use HttpOnly cookies or in-memory
- Implement token revocation for logout and password changes

### Login Security
- Use generic error messages: "Invalid email or password" — never reveal which field is wrong
- Implement account lockout or exponential backoff after failed attempts (e.g., 5 attempts then 15-minute lock)
- Rate-limit login endpoints at the IP and account level
- Log all authentication events (success and failure) with IP and timestamp
- Support MFA — TOTP at minimum; push/WebAuthn preferred

### Password Policy
- Minimum 8 characters (NIST 800-63B recommends allowing up to 64+)
- Check against breached password lists (Have I Been Pwned API or local list)
- Do not force arbitrary complexity rules (uppercase/special char) — length matters more
- Allow paste into password fields (do not disable)

### Examples

#### Python (bcrypt)
```python
import bcrypt

# Hash
hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12))

# Verify
if bcrypt.checkpw(password.encode(), hashed):
    # authenticated
```

#### Node.js (bcrypt)
```javascript
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';

// Hash
const hash = await bcrypt.hash(password, 12);

// Verify
const match = await bcrypt.compare(password, hash);
```

#### Go (bcrypt)
```go
import "golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"

// Hash
hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), 12)

// Verify
err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword(hash, []byte(password))
```
